pages.title: Install and activate
pages.lead: Install the free plugin from your WordPress admin.

steps.text: In WordPress admin, open Plugins. Click Add New Plugin.
The free plugin is in the WordPress plugin directory: search for ILM Size Chart and click Install Now. Here we install it from its zip file with Upload Plugin.
Choose the zip file and click Install Now. WordPress uploads it and says: plugin installed successfully.
Click Activate Plugin. ILM Size Chart is active, and the Size Charts menu is added on the left.

pages.title: The size chart list
pages.lead: Find, switch on and off, edit and delete your size charts.
pages.intro: In this video: the size chart list, where every chart of your shop is managed.

steps.text: In WordPress admin, open the ILM Size Chart menu. The list shows every chart with its ID, its title and its priority.
Shown as tells you how the shopper sees it: Popup is a button that opens a window, On page is a chart directly on the product page.
Display rules lists on which products it is shown: here one selected product. A chart without a rule says: not shown.
The search box finds a chart by its title, its ID or its rule. Type Mug, and the list shows only the mug chart.
The cross clears the search. Per page sets how many charts one page of the list shows.
The status is a switch. Enabled means the chart is shown in the shop. Click it to disable the chart.
Now it says Disabled. The chart and its design are kept, but no product shows it. Click again to enable it.
It is enabled again.
The pencil opens the chart to edit it. The next videos show every tab of that form.
The magic wand opens the same chart with the AI design assistant, which changes it from a sentence you type. It has its own video.
The bin deletes a chart. You are always asked first, because a deleted chart cannot be brought back.
Cancel keeps it. To stop showing a chart for a while, disable it instead of deleting it.
Add Size Chart starts a new chart, and Create with AI builds one for you in three steps.

pages.title: Your first size chart
pages.lead: Create a chart, fill a table, choose the product, and see it in the shop.
pages.intro: In this video: your first size chart, from an empty form to the Size Chart button on the product page.

steps.text: In WordPress admin, open the ILM Size Chart menu. This is the list of your size charts. Click Add Size Chart.
The form opens on the General tab. Give the chart a name. Only you see it, in the list. We call it Men's T-shirts.
Show in: Popup puts a button on the product page that opens the chart in a window. Page shows the chart directly on the page. We keep Popup.
The status is Enabled, so the chart is shown in the shop as soon as you save it.
Now open the Sizechart Designer tab. A new chart is empty.
Click Add Row. A row holds one or more columns, and every column shows one component.
Click to add component. Choose what this place shows: a table, text, an image, a video, tabs or another web page.
We choose Table. The table editor opens with a small sample: the sizes in the first row and one measurement in every row below.
The plus buttons add a column or a row, the minus buttons remove one. We add a column for size XL.
Then type the values: XL, chest 42 inches, waist 36 inches. Every cell is a plain text box.
Click Save in the editor. The table is now in the designer, exactly as the shopper will see it, with an inch and centimetre switch above it.
Last, the Display Rule tab: it decides on which products the chart is shown. We start with Products.
Set Enable Products Rule to Yes, and Show Sizechart to: Selected Products.
Search the product by its name or SKU, and click the search button.
Click the T-shirt in the results. It moves to the list of selected products.
Click Save and stay. The chart is saved and active.
Now the shop. We search for the Hummingbird printed T-shirt and open it. The Size Chart button is on the product page. The Find my size button next to it is a Pro feature with its own video.
The shopper clicks it, and the chart opens in a window.
With CM, every measurement is converted to centimetres. IN switches back.
The cross closes the window. The next videos show every setting of the button, the window and the designer.

pages.title: Show the chart on the page
pages.lead: Popup or directly on the product page, with your own heading and place.
pages.intro: In this video: showing a size chart directly on the product page instead of in a popup, and choosing where it goes.

steps.text: This T-shirt shows its chart as a popup: a button that opens a window. Let us show it directly on the page.
In WordPress admin, edit the T-shirt sizes chart. On the General tab, Show in decides how the chart appears.
Click Page. Two more settings appear. Page display is the heading shown above the chart.
Type the heading. It is shown above the chart on every product that uses it.
Page placement is optional. Leave it empty, and the chart goes to the plugin position, under the add to cart button.
Save and stay, then reload the product page. The chart is now part of the page, with its heading, its unit switch and its table.
To put it somewhere else, type a CSS selector of your theme in Place anywhere. Here: the short description of the product.
Position says where, compared with that element: before it, after it, or inside it at the start or the end. We choose Before Element.
Save again and reload the shop. The chart now sits just before the short description.
Every chart has its own setting, so one product can show a popup while another shows its chart on the page.

pages.title: Status and priority
pages.lead: Which chart a product shows when several charts match it.
pages.intro: In this video: the Status switch, and the Priority that decides which chart wins when several charts match one product.

steps.text: Two charts match our T-shirt: T-shirt sizes, chosen for this product, with priority 10, and Cushion sizes, shown to every product with a certain attribute, with priority 3.
A product shows only one chart: the one with the highest priority. So the T-shirt shows T-shirt sizes.
Edit Cushion sizes. At the bottom of the General tab, set its priority to 20, higher than 10.
Save, and reload the T-shirt. Now the Cushion sizes chart wins.
Status turns a chart off without deleting it. Click Disable.
Save, and the T-shirt is back to T-shirt sizes. A disabled chart is skipped, whatever its priority.
Tip: give specific charts, like one product, a higher priority than general ones, like a whole category.

pages.title: Popup button: text and place
pages.lead: The button title, its direction, alignment and where it goes on the page.
pages.intro: In this video: the size chart button. Its title, its direction, its alignment and its place on the product page.

steps.text: Edit a chart and open the Popup Button tab. At the top is a live preview: a sample product page with your button. Every change shows there at once.
In Button, Basic, type the button title. We write: Check your size. Leave it empty to show only the icon.
Direction turns the button on its side, like a tab on the edge of the page. Vertical, bottom to top.
We go back to Horizontal, the usual look.
Alignment places the button left, center or right in its row. Auto keeps what your theme does. We choose Center.
Location: Module hook position shows the button where the product page prints the plugin, near add to cart.
Next to a page element moves it anywhere: type a CSS selector of your theme, and choose before or after it. We keep the hook position for now.
Margin is the space around the button, padding the space inside it, for top, right, bottom and left.
Save and stay, then open the product in the shop. The button has its new title, and it is centered.

pages.title: Popup button: font and text
pages.lead: Font size, font family, capitals and spacing of the button text.
pages.intro: In this video: the text style of the size chart button.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, then the Text tab of the button.
Font size: we type 17 pixels. The preview grows with it.
Font family: Theme font keeps your shop font, or pick one of the Google Fonts. We choose Montserrat. The shop loads it only on pages that show the button.
Text transform writes it in capitals, small letters, or with a capital on every word. We choose Uppercase.
Letter spacing adds a little air between the letters: one pixel. Line height and text decoration, like underline, are here too.
Save, and the product page shows the same button as the preview.

pages.title: Popup button: colours and border
pages.lead: Colours, border, rounded corners, shadow and the mouse-over look.
pages.intro: In this video: the colours and border of the size chart button, and how it looks when the mouse is over it.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, then Colors and Border. First choose which look you edit: Normal, or Mouse over.
In Normal, set the background colour. Type it or click the swatch to pick one. We use blue, with white text.
Border radius rounds the corners. 24 pixels on every corner gives a pill shape. The border width and colour are next to it.
Now click Mouse over. The preview shows the mouse-over look while you edit it.
We make the background darker on mouse over. Transition duration sets how smoothly it changes.
Save. In the shop, the button is blue and rounded, and it turns darker when the mouse is over it.

pages.title: Popup button: icon
pages.lead: A sample icon or your own image on the button.
pages.intro: In this video: the icon of the size chart button.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, then Icon. Upload your own image, or click one of the samples.
We click the size sample. The preview button shows it at once.
Icon placement puts it before or after the text.
Icon size: 26 pixels. Remove white background helps a picture that has a white square around it.
None removes the icon. We put the sample back, and save.
In the shop, the button shows the icon with its text.

pages.title: Popup window: size and position
pages.lead: How big the window is, where it opens, and what happens with a big chart.
pages.intro: In this video: the size and position of the popup window that shows the chart.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, then Popup Window, Size and Position.
Click Open popup to see the window with your real chart. It stays open while you change the settings.
Width: we type 640 pixels. You can use pixels or percent of the screen. Max width and min width keep it within limits on large and small screens.
Position on screen: the middle, or the top, a side, or the bottom. We choose Top center.
When the chart is bigger than the window, Scroll adds a scroll bar, Visible lets it grow, and Hidden cuts it. Scroll is best for long charts.
Save. In the shop, the window is narrower and opens at the top of the screen.
On phones the window always fits the screen width.

pages.title: Popup window: style and animation
pages.lead: Colours, border, the dimmed page behind it, and how it opens and closes.
pages.intro: In this video: the look of the popup window, the page overlay behind it, and its animations.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, Popup Window, then Style.
We give the window a warm background and rounded corners of 18 pixels, and open the preview. Padding and border are here too.
Page overlay colour and opacity dim the page behind the window: dark blue, at 70 percent.
In Animation, choose how the window opens: fade, slide, zoom or bounce, and its speed in milliseconds. The close animation is set the same way. We choose Zoom.
Open popup plays the animation in the preview.
Save, and the shop opens the chart the same way.
The text colour field sets the colour of all text in the window.

pages.title: Popup window: close button
pages.lead: The button that closes the size chart window.
pages.intro: In this video: the close button of the popup window.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, then Close Button.
We make it red with a white cross, and open the preview to see it.
Width, height and font size set its size. Button text can be a cross or a word like Close.
Offset from corner moves it from the top right corner. A negative value puts it just outside the window.
Save. In the shop, the window has the red close button. Escape and a click on the dimmed page close it too.
The mouse-over look of the close button is set with the Mouse over switch, like the size chart button.

pages.title: Preview on phone and tablet
pages.lead: Check the popup on every screen size, and go back to the default style.
pages.intro: In this video: previewing the popup on desktop, tablet and phone, and the Apply default style button.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open Popup Button, and click Open popup. The bar at the bottom switches the screen size.
Tablet shows the chart as a tablet shopper sees it.
Phone: a narrow screen. Check that the table scrolls well and the text is readable.
Back to desktop. Apply default style puts every button, icon, window and close button setting back to the default look.
You are asked first. Nothing is saved until you click Save, so you can still go back by leaving the page.
We cancel, and keep our design.

pages.title: Designer: rows and columns
pages.lead: Build the layout of your chart: rows, columns and their settings.
pages.intro: In this video: the layout of the Sizechart Designer. Rows, columns, and their settings.

steps.text: Edit a chart and open the Sizechart Designer. This chart has two rows: the table on top, and a row with the measuring tips and a picture.
Point at a row and click its blue button. The row toolbar opens: add a column, add a row, row settings, and delete the row.
Add Column puts a third column in the row. A row takes up to six columns, side by side; on phones they stack.
Each column has a menu: add a component, duplicate the column, hide it, delete it, or open its options.
We delete the empty column again. If a column has content, you are asked first.
Row settings set the spacing, the background colour or picture, the border and the shadow of the whole row. Columns have the same options.
The dotted handle at the top left drags a row up or down. Columns have their own handle.
Undo and Redo take back any change in the designer. Nothing is stored until you save the chart.

pages.title: Table: sizes and measurements
pages.lead: Type your sizes, add rows and columns, or paste a whole table from Excel.
pages.intro: In this video: filling the size table. Typing, adding rows and columns, and pasting from Excel or Google Sheets.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open the designer, and click the table. The table editor opens on the Basic tab.
The green plus at the start of a row adds a row below it. We add Waist, and type a value for every size.
The red minus removes a row; above the table, the same buttons add and remove columns.
Already have the sizes in Excel or Google Sheets? Click Paste from Excel, copy the cells there, and paste them here.
The pasted cells keep their rows and columns.
Replace table content fills the table with them. The style and the units are kept.
Save the editor and the chart. In the shop, the chart shows chest, waist, length and sleeve.
Every cell is plain text, so you can write sizes, ranges or notes, exactly as your shop needs them.

pages.title: Table: units
pages.lead: A centimetre and inch switch, converted for you.
pages.intro: In this video: table units. Type your sizes once, and the shopper switches between centimetres and inches.

steps.text: Edit the chart, click the table in the designer, and open the Units tab.
The first unit is the base unit: the unit you typed the numbers in. Here centimetres, so its conversion value is always 1.
Every other unit has a conversion value: what one base unit is in that unit. One centimetre is 0.3937 inches. The numbers are converted for you; text cells stay as they are.
Add Unit adds another: millimetres. One centimetre is 10 millimetres, so its value is 10. The bin deletes a unit.
Save the editor and the chart. In the shop, the switch has three buttons.
MM shows every measurement in millimetres. The shopper choice is remembered on the next product.
A table with only one unit shows no switch at all.

pages.title: Table: style
pages.lead: Header colours, stripes, lines and the unit buttons.
pages.intro: In this video: the style of the size table.

steps.text: Edit the chart, click the table, and open the Table tab. Its own tabs set the layout, the header, the first column, the body, the lines and the unit buttons.
Layout: header row and first column on or off, the width, the alignment, and a scroll bar for wide tables on phones.
Header: we give the header row a dark orange background. Text colour, font size and spacing are here too.
Body sets the colours of the rows, stripes on every second row, and the colour when the mouse is over a row.
Lines and frame: the border around the table and the lines between the cells.
Save the editor: the designer shows the new header at once. Apply default style, on the Table tab, puts the original look back.
Save the chart, and the shop shows the same table.
For a ready-made look in one click, use Themes. It has its own video.

pages.title: Text editor
pages.lead: Headings, tips and lists next to your table.
pages.intro: In this video: the text editor component, for measuring tips and notes.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open the designer, click Add Row, then Click to add component, and choose Text Editor.
Type your text, like any word processor.
Select the first line and click Bold. The toolbar also has colours, alignment, lists, links, fonts and sizes.
Save the editor. The text is a new row under the chart.
Save the chart. In the shop, the note is shown under the table.
Use the text editor for measuring tips, fit notes or a short care guide next to the table.

pages.title: Image
pages.lead: A measuring guide or a product picture in the chart.
pages.intro: In this video: the image component. Upload a measuring guide and reuse it from the image library.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open the designer, add a row and choose Image.
Click Select. Upload a new picture, or browse the pictures you uploaded before.
We choose a measuring guide from the computer. It is shown before it is uploaded.
Click Upload. The picture is stored in your shop and filled in. Next time it is in the Browse Images tab.
Alt text describes the picture for search engines and for shoppers who use a screen reader.
Save the editor and the chart. The picture is in the size chart in the shop. On the Style tab you can set its size, border and rounded corners.
PNG, JPG, GIF and WebP pictures up to 5 megabytes can be uploaded.

pages.title: Video
pages.lead: Show a how-to-measure video inside the chart.
pages.intro: In this video: the video component.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open the designer, add a row and choose Video.
Paste the link of the video: a YouTube or Vimeo page.
Width and height set its size. 100 percent fills the column.
Save the editor. The video is shown in its row; the shopper plays it inside the size chart.
Save the chart to keep it. A short video of how to measure answers many questions before they are asked.

pages.title: Tabs
pages.lead: Several tables behind tab titles, like Men and Women.
pages.intro: In this video: the tab component, to put several contents behind tab titles.

steps.text: This sweater shows a chart with three tabs: tops, bottoms and size systems. The shopper clicks a title to see its content.
To make tabs, edit a chart, add a row and choose Tab.
Type the tab titles: Men and Women. Add Tab adds another, the red button removes one.
Save the editor. In the designer, click inside a tab to add its content: a table, text or a picture, like in a column.
Tab Title and Tab Content, in the editor, style the titles in normal, mouse over and selected state, and the content area.

pages.title: Themes
pages.lead: Ready-made looks for your tables, in one click.

video.note: Filmed with the Pro add-on installed. Midnight, used in this video, is one of the 5 Pro themes; the 8 free themes work the same way.

pages.intro: In this video: themes. Ready-made looks for your size chart.

steps.text: Edit the chart, open the designer, and click Themes. Every card shows a sample table in that theme.
Each theme has two buttons. Apply to my tables gives your own tables this look. Add as new row adds a complete sample block in this theme.
We click Apply to my tables on Midnight. A bar asks to confirm, and says how many tables change.
Yes. The table has the Midnight colours; its content and units are kept.
Not happy? One click on Undo takes the whole theme back.
We keep it and save. The shop shows the new look.
The option Also style the popup button and window, in the themes window, matches the button to the theme too.

pages.title: Export and import a design
pages.lead: Copy a chart design to another chart or another shop.
pages.intro: In this video: exporting a chart design to a file, and importing it into another chart.

steps.text: Edit the chart and open the designer. Export and Import are in the designer toolbar.
Export downloads the whole design as a small file: rows, columns, tables, texts, pictures and styles.
Now open another chart, here a new one, and click Import in its designer.
Choose the exported file. The same design is loaded into this chart.
This also copies a design from a test shop to your live shop. Give the chart a title and display rules, and save it.

pages.title: Display rule: categories
pages.lead: Show one chart on every product of a category.
pages.intro: In this video: showing a size chart on whole categories, so new products get it automatically.

steps.text: This T-shirt is in the category Men, and no size chart is shown for it yet.
Edit the Size guide chart, open Display Rule, then Categories. The rule is on, for the selected category Women.
All Categories would show it on every product of the shop. Selected Categories limits it to the list below.
Search for Men, and click the search button.
Click Men in the results. Now the chart is for both categories. A product counts when one of its categories is in the list. Child categories are included.
Save, and reload the T-shirt. It now shows the Size guide chart, on the page, because that chart is set to Page.
The Delete button takes a category off the list again. Every product added to these categories later shows the chart too.

pages.title: Display rule: brands and tags
pages.lead: Show a chart on every product of a brand or with a tag.
pages.intro: In this video: size charts by brand and by product tag.

steps.text: Edit the Print sizes chart, open Display Rule, then Brands. The rule is on, for the brand Graphic Corner.
Search and click a brand to add it, the same way as products and categories. Every product of these brands shows this chart.
In the shop, this framed poster is made by Graphic Corner, so it shows the print sizes.
Tags work the same way. The Mug sizes chart is shown for products with the tag accessories-supplier.
So this mug, which has that tag, shows the mug sizes, with a millilitre and fluid ounce switch.
A brand or tag rule is handy when one maker or one product line always uses the same sizes.

pages.title: Display rule: attributes
pages.lead: Show a chart on every product with an attribute.
pages.intro: In this video: size charts by product attribute.

steps.text: Edit the Cushion sizes chart, open Display Rule, then Attributes. The rule is on, for the attribute Property.
Every product that uses this global attribute shows the chart. Search and click to add more attributes.
In the shop, the Brown bear cushion has that attribute, so it shows the cushion sizes.
Attributes are useful when products of many categories share one type of size, like fabric or material.

pages.title: Display rule: Any or All
pages.lead: When a chart has several rules: one of them, or all of them.
pages.intro: In this video: Apply Constrain. What happens when one chart has several display rules.

steps.text: The Mug sizes chart has a tag rule: the tag accessories-supplier. Notebooks and cushions have that tag too.
We add a second rule: Categories, Home Accessories, where the mugs are.
With two rules on, a new tab appears: Apply Constrain. Any shows the chart when one rule matches. The other button needs every rule to match.
With Any, a notebook with the same tag matches the tag rule, so it shows the mug sizes. That is not what we want.
So we choose the second button: the product must match the tag and the category.
Save. The notebook is not a home accessory, so it shows its own notebook chart again. The mugs still show the mug sizes.
Use Any to add up rules, and All to narrow them down.

pages.title: Shortcode
pages.lead: Show a size chart on any page or post.
pages.intro: In this video: the ilm size chart shortcode, to show a size chart outside the product page, for example on a size guide page.

steps.text: Open Pages, Add New Page, and give it a title. We make a size guide page for our T-shirt.

In the page, type the shortcode: ilm size chart, in square brackets, with product equals the ID of the product. 92 is our T-shirt. You see the product ID in the product list when the mouse is over a product.
Click Publish, check the settings, and click Publish again.
The page is live.
Open the page in the shop. The shortcode shows the T-shirt chart exactly as on the product page: here its Size Chart button.
It opens the same popup, with the same design and unit switch.
Without the product part, the shortcode shows the chart of the current product. That is handy in a product description or a page builder template. Products with no matching chart show nothing.

pages.title: Deactivate and delete
pages.lead: Switch the plugin off, or remove it with its size charts.

video.note: This video also removes the Pro add-on from the demo shop. With the free plugin only, skip those parts: the steps here jump straight to the free plugin.

pages.intro: In this video: deactivating ILM Size Chart, and deleting it completely.

steps.text: Deleting the plugin deletes all size charts and their settings. To keep a design, export it first with Export in the designer.
On the Plugins page, deactivate ILM Size Chart. The shop no longer shows any size chart, but nothing is deleted yet.
Then delete ILM Size Chart. This also deletes its size charts, settings and uploaded pictures. To use it again, install it as shown in the install video.
